test(Core::IO::Stream&) uses void as an explicit unresolved original ordinary return declaration. Parameter identity is preserved. No original test return-type readiness claim.
Native old Stream slot16 read and slot12 seek are named source-adapted to actual pinned CCL readBytes and setPosition; no original Core instructions are emulated or reconstructed.

Successful factory allocations and live borrowed providers only. Streams terminate both passes with zero. A nonzero negative result is retained and uint8-truncated; every byte consumed by that truncation must already be initialized. The bounded -1 fixture fills256 bytes independently before returning -1. Uninitialized/error-provider domains and nonterminating streams are excluded.

Native queue/MIDI/factory boundaries are serviced by existing canonical portable provider implementations, independently of new endpoint code. This validates endpoint native control/call effects with those providers, not original queue ARM semantics. Existing MIDI malformed/short and ownership regressions are replayed separately from new endpoint reconstruction.

Original C1 and C2 ranges differ in branch encoding/address and are verified/executed separately; host compiler emits aliased C1/C2 addresses, both directly invoked. Both native D1 ranges are checked/executed separately, write the same DataChannel vptr only and do not free or flush borrowed queues. Host source lifecycle preserves borrowed queue bytes and observes actual D0 deallocation. Persistent dead-object vptr bytes are explicitly not a portable source guarantee; the optimized base destructor may omit the native-style store.

Native D0 branch is bound through exact ELF PLT relocation to _ZdlPv. Its observed guest delete boundary removes/unmaps a live guest allocation; native allocator internals are not executed. Host D0 calls real operator delete/free and is observed before deallocation. No selected original endpoint D2 nor DataChannel D0 credit.

The earlier post-destruction host vptr assertion was rejected by canonical Release integration: optimized DataChannel D1 is ret, while UBSan clears dead vptr bytes. Both dead-storage expectations were removed. Exact original native table stores remain mandatory, host C1/C2/D1 calls preserve actual borrowed queue bytes, and D0 must truly deallocate. Rejected seals/logs and canonical disassembly are preserved in rejected-seal-01 and optimized-failure.json; mixed Release production/O0 driver replay is required.
No hardware, flashing, guest syscalls, exception/allocation-failure or full Linux integration/role/archive/readiness admission is claimed locally. Root retains those gates.
